name: Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) (C0017)

techniques.comment: Removing Cossack regiments from the Cossack hierarchy and placing them under the direct command of imperial officials: Peter I handed the direction of the Ladoga Canal works to B.-C. Münnich, who "took over from Prince A. Menshikov the direction of the construction (digging) of the Ladoga Canal"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 6 2009); Cossack corps were dispatched to these works "by order of Tsar Peter I"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

The mass mobilization of Cossack regiments for penal construction labor: the digging of the Ladoga Canal "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and there "tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 6 2009). In 1721 a "10,000-strong Cossack corps" headed by P. Polubotok was dispatched to the canal(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011); the works continued through 1721–23(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012).

Shifting the upkeep of the mobilized onto the subjects themselves: Cossacks dispatched to the imperial construction sites were left without supply and "suffer great want from hunger, having neither food for themselves, nor winter quarters, nor fodder for the horses"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011). Workers for state construction the tsar simply ordered to be "taken from Ukraine, from those towns that are under your authority"(Citation: Иван Мазепа и Российская империя. История «предательства» 2011), while at the works themselves people perished "from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 6 2009).
